motivation: In 1997 Maldacena proposed that quantum gravity in anti-de Sitter space is exactly equivalent to a gauge theory on its boundary. Polyakov (with Gubser and Klebanov) and Witten turned the conjecture into a precise dictionary relating bulk fields to boundary operators and correlation functions. The duality gives a non-perturbative definition of quantum gravity in which black hole evaporation is unitary. It has passed a very large number of exact tests: integrability spectra, localization, superconformal indices, and the microscopic counting of the entropy of supersymmetric AdS black holes from gauge theory. It has also become a working tool for strongly coupled systems, from quark-gluon plasma viscosity to quantum chaos and entanglement, where the Ryu-Takayanagi formula ties spacetime geometry to quantum information. Few ideas since quantum field theory itself have changed so much of how physicists understand gravity, gauge dynamics and strong coupling.
